title: Model & Route Observability — Dashboard Redesign and Chart Spec
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a compact, actionable Model & Route performance dashboard that surfaces latency (p50/p90/p99), throughput (RPS), token metrics (tokens/request, tokens/min), and cost signals, with easy comparison across model variants and rollout annotations. This ticket captures the UI/interaction design, high-fidelity prototype links, and detailed chart specs needed for implementation and review.

Scope: Per-model card view + per-route detail page. Main components: overview KPI strip, time-series charts (latency quantiles, throughput, tokens), distribution histograms (tokens/request), SLO overlays, rollout & deploy event annotations, compare mode (baseline vs variant), and export/alert hooks. Not in scope: backend aggregation work (ENG tickets), custom report builder (future).

Design constraints & principles: Compact at top level (card grid) to scale to 50+ models; progressive disclosure into detailed route view; prioritize temporal alignment across charts (shared time window and brush); show percentiles instead of raw raw traces by default to reduce noise; accessible color palette and patterns for color-blind users.

Prototype links: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/console-observability-v2?node-id=402%3A1 (main prototype)
Design spec doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xY_prototype_spec (chart spec & accessibility notes)
Visual tokens: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/observability-design-assets
Engineering PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/812

Acceptance criteria: 
- Overview shows model-level KPIs and sparklines for p50/p90 latency, RPS, and tokens/min for selected time window.
- Clicking a model opens the route-level detail page with synchronized charts.
- Latency chart shows at minimum p50, p90, p99 lines plus median band shading; tooltip shows exact values and request counts.
- Tokens chart provides sum(tokens) per minute and histogram of tokens/request for the selected period.
- SLO overlay can be toggled on/off and renders as dashed threshold line at configured value.
- Rollout/deploy annotations appear as vertical markers with summary on hover and link to rollout detail.
- Export CSV button for time-series and download of raw sampled rows.
- Designs include microcopy for cost-per-1k tokens and explainers for quantiles.

Chart-level spec highlights (see also attached spec document):
- Default time ranges: 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d. Default: 6h.
- Downsampling/rollup: backend should provide 1m rollups for <=24h, 5m rollups for <=7d, 1h rollups for >7d. UI will show a small notice when viewing >30d stating values are aggregated.
- Latency chart: multi-series line chart with series: p50 (solid), p90 (solid), p99 (dashed). Aggregation function: percentile over request latencies per rollup bucket. Y-axis linear ms (auto-scale). Hover shows bucket time, percentile values, request count. Legend supports toggling series visibility.
- Throughput chart: area chart for requests per second (RPS) and stacked bar for error counts. Aggregation: sum(requests)/bucket-duration. Secondary axis for error rate percent.
- Tokens chart: dual-axis: top axis tokens/min as line, bottom axis avg tokens/request as points. Also supply tokens/request histogram (log-binned) as separate small chart.
- Distribution histograms: show sample count, median, IQR. Toggle between linear/log scale.
- Comparison mode: allow selecting up to 3 model variants or time ranges; charts overlay with distinct color & opacity and a small diff summary panel showing relative cost and latency changes.
- Annotations: event type enum [deploy, rollout, incident, maintenance]; each has color and icon. Clicking an annotation opens a small panel with links to PR/incident runbook.

Data & performance notes for engineers:
- For long ranges, prefer pre-aggregated store. Sampling guidelines documented in ENG-2034.
- Client-side downsampling should not compute percentiles; rely on server computed quantiles to avoid misrepresentation.
- For histograms, request a pre-computed histogram or TDigest payload.

Accessibility & UX trade-offs:
- Use high-contrast color pairs and dashed line patterns for p99 to remain readable in grayscale.
- Keep tooltip content concise; include copy for screen reader announcements on chart focus so non-visual users can understand key KPIs.

Open design questions: 
- Should we show per-route sparklines on the model card by default or only top-5 routes? (PM leaning: show model-level only; add quick expand to show top-5 routes)
- Exact quantile set: p50/p90/p99 vs p75/p95? (initial consensus: p50/p90/p99 for production SLOs; include p95 as optional toggle)
- How to surface cost deltas for multi-model requests where a route calls multiple models? (follow-up with billing team and PM-402)

Next steps: 
1) Resolve open questions in design critique (see comments).
2) Finalize high-fidelity frames for route detail and export states.
3) Hand-off chart spec file and figma tokens to ENG PRs.

Estimated implementation notes (for planning): front-end charting work (shared chart component updates) + back-end endpoints for rollups/histograms (ENG-2034) + rollout annotation API (ENG-2101).

decision_log: 2026-02-22: Agreed on default percentiles p50/p90/p99, with p95 as optional toggle.
2026-02-23: Default overview time window set to 6h for low-noise UX; users can change to wide ranges as needed.
2026-02-24: Comparison mode limited to 3 series to preserve readability and performance.
